source.title: Necessary and sufficient graphical conditions for optimal adjustment sets in causal graphical models with hidden variables
source.location: Supplement Appendix B.10, pp. 18-21, proof of Theorem 3, sufficiency ("if") half; both examined passages sit on p. 19. Pagination is that of the 41-page arXiv v4 PDF. Line numbers refer to the arXiv v4 LaTeX source Runge_Optimal_adjustment_sets_v5_neurips.tex, whose lines 1156-1267 are that subsection.
source.transcription: Graphs constructed here, not transcribed from the paper. Case 1 refutes a published proof step with its hypotheses in force; case 2 refutes only a hypothesis-free reading; case 3 refutes an attempted repair, not a claim of the paper.
source.adjudication: Each case was adjudicated against two independent implementations: this library for the O-set, Conditions (I) and (II) and the optimality verdict, and a separate definition-level implementation of m-separation and adjustment validity written from the published definitions. The two agree on every field recorded here.
source.scope: These observations do not establish a counterexample to the statement of Theorem 3 or to the implementation. On every case the library verdict agrees with a separate evaluation of the graphical criterion; finite agreement does not prove its distributional equivalence. THE THREE CASES ARE NOT OF EQUAL FORCE: case 1 is a counterexample to a step with its hypotheses in force; case 2 refutes only a hypothesis-free reading of a step, since Condition (II) is false on that graph, and leaves open whether the step is complete on its own terms; case 3 refutes a repair one might attempt, not a claim of the paper.

cases.reported: In the branch where N-nodes exist, term (iii') = I(R;Y|BX) is said to be non-zero only if Z' contains a descendant of an N-node together with all nodes of one of its collider paths; the step concludes at line 1190 that term (iii') is zero.
cases.adjudicated: False as written. With Z = {U, U2} a valid adjustment set, B = O intersect Z is empty, so the conditioning set of term (iii') is {X} alone, and the path U2 <- V -> Y is open: V is a non-collider lying in O but on the A-side, so it is not conditioned on. No N-node plays any role in this open path. The supporting lemmas the step relies on are stated for conditioning sets containing all of O.
cases.conclusion_survives_via: With the subset witness A' = {V} one has Y m-separated from {U,U2} given {X,V}, so I(R;Y|BX) <= I(A';Y|BX) <= I(A;Y|BX) by the chain rule and non-negativity of conditional mutual information. That step is not in the paper.

cases.reported: Read without its Condition (II) hypothesis, the Case (2) passage asserts that a node E outside the valid ancestors satisfies E m-separated from X given O minus {E}, hence E is not one of the nodes the condition must cover.
cases.adjudicated: That hypothesis-free reading is false: P is not in the valid ancestors {Q}, yet X is m-connected to P given O minus {P} = {C}. IMPORTANT LIMIT OF THIS WITNESS: Case (2) treats nodes whose Condition (II) witnesses are all of type 2, i.e. leaving E by an ARROWHEAD. P has no bidirected edge at all, so it has no type-2 witness; its path P -> C <-> Y leaves P by a tail (type 1) and its collider C is not in the valid ancestors, so it is not an admissible Condition (II) witness either. Condition (II) is therefore FALSE here and the library returns graphical_optimality false. This graph does NOT meet the hypotheses of Case (2) and is NOT a direct counterexample to it. The source invokes Condition (II) at line 1195 to establish the witness typology inherited by Case (2), lines 1199-1210. The absence of another explicit invocation inside that case would not establish that the hypothesis is unused. Whether Case (2) is complete on its own terms is not settled here.
cases.conclusion_survives_via: The repair target is the statement that actually spends the hypothesis: Condition (II), Z valid, E in the E-set and E not in Z imply X m-separated from E given Z. That is weaker than membership of E in Z.
cases.witness_type: type 1 only (tail at E); no type-2 witness exists in this graph

cases.defective_claim_lines: not a claim of the paper; the stronger reading one might attempt as a repair
cases.reported: One natural repair of the Case (2) step would be that Condition (II) forces every E-set node into every valid adjustment set.
cases.adjudicated: False. Conditions (I) and (II) both hold and the O-set is {C, D} with E-set {C}, yet Z = {A} is a valid adjustment set omitting C. The weaker m-separation statement does hold here, X being m-separated from C given {A}.
